workIntro.title: Different brands. The same care.
workIntro.text: A mix of real-world work, independent concepts and a university brand PR project. Each case makes my contribution, the audience and the thinking behind the work clear.

projects.title: A clearer digital front door.
projects.summary: Supporting a local childcare business with parent-friendly social content, Meta advertising and practical website updates.
projects.thumbnailAlt: The childcare website's parent information and gallery.

media.alt: Website content explaining funded childcare and showing the play environment.
media.caption: Selected live website excerpts: useful information and a view of the play environment.

media.alt: Nasima's Childcare social identity with a colourful tree and a play-and-grow message.
media.caption: The business's social identity, included as project context.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.text: Help a small Enfield childcare business present its services clearly to local parents. The content needed to feel reassuring, easy to understand and consistent with the information on its website.

sections.heading: My contribution
items: Created and managed Facebook content and designed posts in Canva.
Ran Meta Facebook Ads Manager campaigns aimed at local parents.
Updated website HTML content and imagery through GitHub, including funded-childcare information.

sections.heading: What this shows
sections.text: Practical marketing support across more than one channel: adapting a message for social, keeping information current and paying attention to the detail that helps a parent take the next step.

note.label: A useful lesson
note.text: Clarity is part of the creative work. For a service like childcare, helpful information and a reassuring tone matter as much as an attractive post.

projects.title: Bringing collections to the feed.
projects.summary: Fashion content and live presenting for a clothing brand, with work across TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube.
projects.thumbnailAlt: A face-free crop showing the embroidery and blue fabric in Anzara's gharara collection video.

media.alt: A face-free detail of the floral embroidery and draped fabric in Anzara's ready-saree video.
media.caption: Garment detail / Ready-saree collection / TikTok / March 2023

media.alt: A face-free detail of an embellished gharara outfit and flowing blue fabric from Anzara's collection video.

sections.heading: The context
sections.text: Collection content had to make the clothing feel engaging beyond a still product image. Short-form formats and livestreams offered different ways to show the garments and connect with viewers.

sections.heading: My contribution
items: Created fashion content and short-form videos for the brand's social channels.
Hosted livestreams and presented collections to an online audience.
Worked with formats including Reels, Stories, TikToks, YouTube videos and Facebook video.

sections.heading: What this shows
sections.text: Confidence communicating a product's appeal, familiarity with platform-specific content and experience working as part of a brand's wider production effort.

note.label: Content in context
note.text: Created with Anzara's wider team; my contribution was content creation and presenting. Public TikTok view counts checked on 9 October 2026. The figures refer to these two videos, not an average across all my work.

projects.title: An idea with a natural flow.
projects.summary: A flowing-hair visual that turns a simple seasonal message into a recognisable beauty concept.
projects.thumbnailAlt: Flora beauty concept in navy and white, with hair flowing like a waterfall.

media.alt: A navy flowing-hair illustration alongside the headline 'Let your summer style flow' and the Flora logo.
media.caption: An independent Canva concept, with the headline refined for this portfolio.

sections.heading: The creative challenge
sections.text: Give a local beauty business a simple, distinctive seasonal social post. I wanted the image and the words to work together rather than compete for attention.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.text: The hair becomes a waterfall: a visual metaphor for movement and flow. A restrained navy-and-white palette keeps the silhouette and brand name easy to recognise.

sections.heading: How I'd develop it
sections.text: Pair the awareness post with a service-led Story and a clear booking link. I would test the message against a treatment-led version and compare booking-link clicks, not just likes.

note.label: From concept to next step
note.text: The original Canva idea is mine. This portfolio version refines the headline to 'Let your summer style flow'. The suggested rollout and measurement are proposals, not delivered campaign results.

projects.title: Let the product idea bloom.
projects.summary: A dress silhouette grows from a flower, connecting a summer message to the product category in one glance.
projects.thumbnailAlt: Green-and-white Boden concept with a flower turning into a dress silhouette.

media.alt: A green flower-and-dress illustration with the headline 'Let your style bloom this summer' and the Boden name.
media.caption: An independent summer concept exploring the connection between flowers, dresses and seasonal style.

sections.heading: The creative challenge
sections.text: Create a memorable seasonal fashion post without relying on a busy layout. The idea needed to communicate summer and clothing immediately.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.text: The flower and dress share one silhouette, giving 'bloom' a visual meaning. Green, white space and a short headline make the concept feel fresh and easy to scan.

sections.heading: How I'd develop it
sections.text: Extend the concept into a product-led carousel using approved collection photography, ending with a 'Shop summer dresses' call to action. I would compare product-page clicks and saves across the creative versions.

note.label: Clear project status
note.text: This is a self-initiated creative exercise, not work commissioned, approved or published by Boden. The proposed extension is a next-step idea, not a campaign result.

projects.title: Making a big message feel approachable.
projects.summary: A two-sided brochure concept exploring how a playful brand voice can make an environmental message more engaging for a Gen Z audience.
projects.thumbnailAlt: Colourful Cheeky Panda university brochure artwork in green, orange and yellow.

media.alt: Front of the academic brochure, combining panda illustrations, environmental messaging and a 'Join us in taking action' headline.
media.caption: Brochure front: a campaign hook, a brand message and an invitation to act.

media.alt: Reverse of the academic brochure, organised into 'Why does it matter?', 'What you can do' and 'What we're doing' panels.
media.caption: Brochure reverse: three clear message sections, cropped for the portfolio.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.text: Create a university brand PR concept for The Cheeky Panda, balancing an environmental theme with the brand's playful personality and a young audience.

sections.heading: My contribution
sections.text: Created the brochure concept in Canva, combining panda illustrations, bold green-and-orange sections, explanatory copy and calls to action across two sides.

sections.heading: What this shows
sections.text: Thinking beyond a single social post: organising a longer message, adapting brand tone and building a visual sequence from an opening idea to a reader action.

note.label: An academic concept
note.text: This university exercise was not commissioned or approved by The Cheeky Panda. The draft copy is illustrative, not a statement of verified environmental performance; its claims would need checking before a real campaign.
